subject.title: docs(cli): generate and guard command reference

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a new core `commands` CLI root and expanded plugin CLI descriptor metadata as a permanent public contract, or keep command-reference generation outside the core catalog stack?
rationale: The branch adds a public CLI surface and plugin metadata fields rather than repairing an established broken contract; this requires maintainer direction independent of implementation quality.

options.title: Sponsor the catalog contract
options.body: Confirm the `commands` root and descriptor metadata as supported interfaces, then require narrowed implementation and exact-head proof before merge.

options.title: Keep docs static and hand-authored
options.body: Reject the new catalog/API surface and retain the existing CLI documentation workflow.

options.title: Move the experiment out of core
options.body: Direct the inventory workflow to an external plugin or experimental surface until the core API direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the catalog contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the `commands` root and descriptor metadata as supported interfaces, then require narrowed implementation and exact-head proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline shows direct review attention, while no repository-history inspection was available to identify a stronger current-main owner.
